milestone: MSCA-DN historical validation, ticket V03 (Name and green the PE-09 acceptance lane) in plans/msca_dn_historical_validation_tickets.md; closes finding F08 of plans/reports/MSCA_DN_Readiness_Audit_2026-10-08.md
authority: CLAUDE.md §9.4 (a decision that affects future interpretation is written to Tier 4), §9.5 (an output is reproducible from its documented inputs, or at minimum auditable), §12.1 (an output names its inputs and flags its assumptions), §12.2 (the four status categories), §12.4 (a missing mandatory input triggers a declared failure), §15 (a declared gap over a fabricated completion). Ticket V03. Not a constitutional amendment.
decision: The acceptance lane is declared as twelve named coverage areas rather than a list of test paths, and one command runs it: py -3.10 -m harness.commands.acceptance_lane. The declaration is data, at harness/acceptance_lanes/msca_dn_historical.json; harness/acceptance_lane.py reads it and carries no instrument name of its own, the same separation harness/profile.py keeps from its profiles. The prose declaration is harness/ACCEPTANCE_LANE.md and the guards are tests/harness/test_acceptance_lane.py. The lane reconciles each run against the declaration in both directions: a skip no exclusion declares fails it as an undeclared skip, and a declared exclusion the run never reports fails it as a stale exclusion. Any failure or setup error fails it. An extraction build not measured to reproduce the committed import artifacts refuses the run, and --allow-unreproducing-build stamps the result NOT CERTIFIED rather than relaxing the check.
why: The audit's own finding is that test counts are not coverage of acceptance invariants: 1,864 cases passed at ca0a443 while four reproduced defects stood. A path list cannot answer which invariant covers the importer; named areas can. The two-directional reconciliation is what stops the exclusion list rotting into either an invisible exclusion or a stale claim, which is the specific failure mode the shared constraint against reporting an exclusion as a pass is written to prevent.

why_the_declaration_is_data.basis: tests/harness/test_profile.py::TestNoInstrumentLiterals, which the lane's first draft failed
why_the_declaration_is_data.reason: A lint over every harness/**/*.py forbids an instrument name outside the profile loader, which is how CLAUDE.md §2 project-agnosticism is held at the code layer. The lane's subject is one instrument's acceptance run, so the first draft carried the instrument name in Python and the lint caught it. Moving the declaration to JSON satisfies the lint by construction rather than by exemption: a second instance declares a second lane and the reader does not change. Weakening the lint to admit the module was considered and rejected.

what_the_lanes_first_run_found.basis: the first complete run of the lane on this checkout

findings.detail: harness/DATASET_DISPOSITIONS.md named test_expectations.py::TestRealSubstrate::test_golden_paths_resolve, and the class had been renamed to TestCriterionSectionMap. The row matched nothing, so the exclusion read as declared while the skip read as undeclared. The lane reported both halves.
findings.resolution: The row was corrected in both documents and in the declaration. A new test asserts that every exclusion names a class its module actually defines, which is the check that was missing: tests/harness/test_dataset_dispositions.py verified only that the module existed.

findings.finding: an instrument literal in harness Python
findings.detail: The lane's own first draft failed the agnosticism lint described above.
findings.resolution: The declaration moved to JSON and the reader became generic.

what_the_lanes_first_run_found.note: Both findings are the lane working as V03 intends. A count-only suite would have reported neither: the skip was already skipping and the row was already written.
